articles.title: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.
articles.body_text: Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers. Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them. As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works toward a particular goal on your behalf. For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project. Other examples Meta gives are a holiday gift tracker, a wedding planner, or a space for DIY projects. “Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that’s a tracker, a planner or a project board,” Meta says. Spaces can also be easily integrated with third-party apps and information, Meta says. “Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask,” the company says. On Friday, Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s founder and CEO, posted about the new feature on X: “Playing around with spaces in Muse lately — tell Muse what you need and it builds it. I’ve made a BBQ game, an event tracker, and a home control dashboard. Excited to see what you build.” Muse agents — and the cuddly avatars that enclose them — have been greeted with a relatively warm reception over the past few months. During its earnings call in October, Zuckerberg said that its agents had 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada — less than two months after the agents debuted. The company is obviously busy building out the user experience around the agents. Spaces is actually the second new Muse feature that Meta has debuted over the last week. On Thursday, the company also announced Muse Voice , which allows users to video chat with their agent and give it commands verbally. The company is in competition with other cute and cuddly AI agents — including OpenAI’s dots and SpaceXAI’s Grokbot , which were debuted with similarly cartoonish personas. articles.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
articles.body_text: Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month. As Anthropic gears up for its IPO , the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed. “Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.” Kharazian said he’s already seeing evidence that the top 1% of firms — the most “ AI-pilled ” — have stuttered slightly in their spend in August and September, coming up just below the $10,000 per-employee they were hitting at their summer peaks. A slowdown among that cohort is “sufficient to slow down revenue entirely, despite the fact that we’re seeing rising volumes,” he said. Ramp data shows growth in spending among median and top 10%, but it’s not enough to make up the difference. Median firms spend $12-$15 per employee per month, and the top 10% spend $600-$1,000. “If you look at the use cases today, it’s not necessarily clear they will get up to that $10,000 per employee per month mark that the 1% is at,” Kharazian said. While there’s plenty of demand for AI coding agents in industries like software and finance, “it’s not necessarily true that a doctor’s office or a car dealership will need to spend that much on AI.” “The era of hypergrowth may be over, and now that we know there may not be as much juice to squeeze out of the top 1%,” he continued. October data did see a re-acceleration, with token spend up 8.9% from September 23 to October 23, but Kharazian said the headwinds on spend growth are strong. Kharazian (who has published a series of blogs called “ Cracks in the AI Thesis ”) said the slowdown isn’t due to a demand problem. Again, AI volumes are up. Instead he points to the competitive nature of the marketplace. “OpenAI and Anthropic price cuts have…just made it cheaper to use AI,” he said. In September, OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Answering the price war, Anthropic has also made significant reductions to pricing for Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 — a decision that the company said in a recent filing slashed revenue growth by about $600 million. Both companies have also been offering enterprise discounts that are intended to lock-in spend, but in reality are hitting their revenue targets. Kharazian said this dynamic means it has very much become a buyer’s market.

articles.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The decision to wind down the EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. Elon Musk said the company will use the factory space to make more Cybercabs.
articles.body_text: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis. The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years. Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions. The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.) This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots. First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a product that Musk had long obsessed over. “Probably my personal favorite for the next product is the pickup truck, and we are going to just do an amazing pickup truck,” he said on one of Tesla’s earnings calls that year. Musk promised the Cybertruck would be radical, inspired by the designs of cyberpunk sci-fi stories like “Blade Runner.” While that certainly bore out in the design, the company overpromised on the basics of the Cybertruck from the jump. During the now-infamous reveal event in 2019, when head designer Franz von Holzhausen cracked the Cybertruck’s windows with steel balls, Tesla said the EV was supposed to start at under $40,000 and have up to 500 miles of range. It achieved neither of those figures. Instead, the truck was delayed for two years, in part because of the COVID-19 pandemic. When it finally did hit the market in late 2023, Tesla handed over the first few Cybertrucks to customers in a short, somewhat odd for Tesla event (by the company’s own standards, at least), which saw a poorly-lit Musk standing in a truck bed promising the truck was “the finest in apocalyptic equipment” fit for “late civilization vibes.” The base price had inflated to around $60,000, and the top-end range had shrunk by over 100 miles. The truck has struggled on the market ever since. The polarizing design never seemed to sit well with buyers, especially at a higher-than-expected price. Then, during its first full year of sales in 2024, Musk became a major financial backer of Donald Trump, which turned the instantly recognizable Cybertruck into a target for protesters. That continued into 2025 as Musk led the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, which fired thousands of federal workers. articles.title: At least 10 local governments have moved to drop Flock’s surveillance cameras since summer | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The concerns range from privacy to how data is shared (and with whom) to procurement concerns.
articles.body_text: Flock, founded in 2017, sells surveillance software that can help solve crimes, such as finding missing people or stolen cars. Its products include license plate readers, drones, and microphone-based edge-computing devices to pick up gunshots and other sounds. More than 100,000 Flock cameras are in use nationwide. But in the past three months, Monroe , Ohio; Newburgh , New York; Richmond , Virginia; Hopkinton, Massachusetts; New Bedford , Massachusetts; and Lansing , Michigan, have all moved to end their contracts with Flock. Meanwhile, police in East Bridgewater and Grafton, Massachusetts, also announced plans to stop using Flock cameras. Just this week, residents of League City, Texas, voted against their police department’s continued use of Flock’s license plate readers, and the cameras are now set to be removed. In Asheville, North Carolina, police lost access to Flock after the city voted to terminate its contract in August, and the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office in Colorado announced in September that it would stop using Flock cameras. When asked for comment, the El Paso County Sheriff’s Office redirected TechCrunch to its press release, where Sheriff Joseph Roybal said that discontinuing the use of Flock was the right decision for the county. “We have the tools, training, and experience to locate and apprehend criminals without relying on Flock cameras,” he said in the press release. Misuse has been a real problem. In August, for example, an officer in Brentwood, Missouri was accused of using Flock cameras to stalk his ex-wife during their divorce. In September, an officer from East Texas was sentenced to prison for using Flock to stalk his ex-girlfriend and her family. Another growing concern is how immigration officials have been able to access the technology. One case that captures the issue came in March, when Ithaca, New York, passed a resolution to terminate its contract with the Flock Group. In the resolution, the city said there were “proven instances of Flock Safety infrastructure being used by federal agents for information purposes even without specific authorizations from the contracting locality,” and that the city had reviewed reports that “either intentionally or through its negligence,” Flock had allowed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) to “use query results from its database of state and local ALPR [automatic license plate reader] data to investigate and persecute immigrants throughout the United States.” “Every day, police departments across the country are using Flock technology to solve serious crimes, locate suspects, find missing people, and make a measurable impact on public safety,” Flock told TechCrunch in a statement. “While we respect every community’s decision, removing a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes and protect communities moves public safety backward. Every Flock customer owns its data and controls who it is shared with and how it can be used. Flock does not sell data and does not have a contract with ICE.” This August, Flock announced it would shorten the default period it stores data for new customers, from 30 days to seven. It also said agencies now need a case code before they can search the database. That lack of awareness is similar to how data centers are popping up across the country, often before residents understand what is happening. Schwartz said police departments often decide to use Flock on their own, with little oversight from city councils. In South Windsor , Connecticut, according to local reports, Flock cameras went live last year without public warning or a vote. In October, the town voted to remove its Flock cameras. “Grassroots activists across the country have been demanding that city councils exercise their procurement power to refuse to pay for ALPRs,” Schwartz said, referring to councils’ power to decide what the city buys. He added that activists have been fighting for years and that “many city councils are listening.” The main argument for technology like Flock is that it helps combat crime and keep neighborhoods safe. And many local governments are not dropping Flock or similar technology; instead, they are adding restrictions on its use or looking for alternatives.

articles.title: 3D DRAM created by IBM and Micron, 128GBps memory on the way
articles.summary: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GB transfer speed scould be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron, using stacked chips and TSVs.
articles.body_text: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GBps transfer speeds could be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron. The companies have developed three-dimensional memory, stacking individual DRAM chips vertically that would normally have to be placed side-by-side, though the efficiencies gained aren’t solely down to space. Communication between the stacked chips and the host device is achieved through a new creation known as through-silicon vias, or TSVs, which run vertically through the pile of chips and act as conduits to the host device. Thanks to the TSVs, in testing the memory has reached data speeds of 128GBps, ten times faster than current memory. On top of this, IBM claims the chips are 70 percent more power efficient than today’s DRAM. The new research is expected to form a key part of Samsung and Micron’s Hybrid Memory Cube technology, first announced back in October. IBM and Micron hope to have commercial availability in two years, with servers likely to use it first. Looking beyond that, IBM fellow Subu Iyer said that the new process “will have applications beyond memory, enabling other industry segments as well.” What exactly those new segments are remains to be seen, but we certainly wouldn’t complain if our computers got the kind of speed bump described here.

articles.title: Hela byn skakas av mordet: "Ofattbart”
articles.summary: Mannen som misstänks ha mördats i Föllinge arbetade inomäldreomsorgen och var deltidsbrandman. Enligt prästen Thomas Svedlund var han mycket omtyckt i byn. – Det är en stor chock för många människor, säger han.
articles.body_text: Mannen som misstänks ha mördats i Föllinge arbetade inom äldreomsorgen och var deltidsbrandman. Enligt prästen Thomas Svedlund var han mycket omtyckt i byn. – Det är en stor chock för många människor, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På fredagseftermiddagen larmades polisen om en skadad man vid en adress i Föllinge i Krokoms kommun. Senare under kvällen meddelade polisen att mannen, som var i 30-årsåldern, hade dött och att en misstänkt gärningsman gripits. En mordutredning inleddes. Thomas Svedlund, församlingspräst i Föllinge, berättar att den misstänkt mördade mannen var omtyckt i byn. – I dag har vi haft en öppen kyrka för allmänheten, och det har varit många som har kommit, säger han. Mannen kom som ensamkommande från Afghanistan. – Han lärde sig språket fort, pluggade och började jobba på ett äldreboende och som deltidsbrandman. Thomas Svedlund träffade själv mannen när han höll andakter på äldreboendet. Enligt prästen visste mannen under lång tid inte om han hade någon familj kvar. Men en dag fick han veta att hans mamma och syskon fortfarande levde.

articles.title: Polis skadades – misstänkt försvann
articles.summary: En 25-årig man åtalas för grovt blåljussabotage och grovt våld mot tjänsteman.
articles.body_text: En 25-årig man står åtalad för grovt blåljussabotage och grovt våld mot tjänsteman. Under påskkravallerna i Örebro kastade han ett föremål i huvudet på en polis som fick hjärnskakning och blev sjukskriven i sex veckor, enligt misstankarna. Åtalet har dröjt eftersom mannen varit i Irak i två år. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Våldsamma kravaller utbröt i flera svenska städer påsken 2022 efter att den dansk-svenske politikern fått tillstånd för allmänna sammankomster, där han aviserat att han skulle bränna Koranen. Värst blev våldet i Sveaparken i Örebro. Den ditkommenderade polisstyrkan utsattes för omfattande stenkastning, sparkar och slag från en stor folksamling. 71 poliser skadades. Åtta fick hjärnskakning, tre fick frakturer, och 33 fick muskel- eller ledskador. Minst åtta polisfordon skadades varav fyra eldades upp. Hittills har 181 personer dömts, de allra flesta för grovt sabotage mot blåljusverksamhet. Nu, fyra och ett halvt år senare, har ytterligare en man åtalats. Han åtalas för grovt sabotage mot blåljusverksamhet men också för grovt våld mot tjänsteman, då ett föremål som han ska ha kastat träffade en polismans hjälm. Polismannen fick hjärnskakning och blev sjukskriven i sex veckor, varav två veckor sängliggande. – Jag var ju, vad man kan säga punch drunk eller full en vecka, ungefär innan jag hade full kognitiv förmåga, har polismannen sagt i förhör. 25-åringen identifierades efter att polisen hösten 2023 publicerat bilder på ännu okända gärningsmän och vädjat om tips från allmänheten. Men när polisen sökte honom på hans adress var han inte där. Han hade flyttat till Irak med fru och barn. I april 2024 blev han efterlyst. Den 10 oktober i år reste han via Istanbul till Oslo och åkte sen i sin pappas bil till Sverige. I Karlstad stoppades bilen och mannen greps.

articles.title: Nordlig kyla på väg – varningen
articles.summary: Brrr! Kallare luft från norr är på väg in ner över landet. Då kan det bli halt på vägarna.
articles.body_text: Kallare luft från norr är på väg in ner över landet. – Det kan vara bra att hålla sig uppmärksam i trafiken, säger SMHI:s meteorolog Emma Härenstam. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Hösten är ett faktum, och snart sveper en rejäl portion kyla in över landet. Helgen och början av nästa vecka präglas av ett högtryck med sol och temperaturer över det normala för årstiden längst upp i norr. Men i mitten av veckan försvinner högtrycket och ersätts av kyligare luft och nederbörd på flera håll i landet. – I och med att det är lite kyligare skulle det kunna vara snöfall så långt söderut som kanske ner till Dalarna ungefär, säger Emma Härenstam, meteorolog på SMHI . Längre söderut blir det blött i form av regn från och med torsdag och in under helgen, även om prognoserna för veckoslutet ännu är lite osäkra. Temperaturen lär inte sträcka sig över femgradersstrecket på särskilt många håll, och Norrland kan förvänta sig minusgrader både natt- och dagtid. I de södra delarna av landet, Götaland och Svealand, för den kalla men fuktiga luften med sig en risk. – Det kan röra sig om frosthalka på sina håll, så det kan vara bra att hålla sig uppmärksam i trafiken. Om termometern visar nära eller under noll och det dessutom är dis och dimma så kan det vara frostavlagring på vägarna. Så det kan vara bra att ha med sig om man ska ge sig ut, säger Emma Härenstam. articles.title: Gabrielsson: ”Förstår oron och besvikelsen”

articles.body_text: Fredagens besked från SD, C och M har förändrat spelplanen i regeringsbildningen. V-toppen Ida Gabrielsson säger att hon ”förstår oron och besvikelsen” – efter Centerpartiets öppning för en borgerlig regering. ”V önskar att vi rödgröna gjort mer”, skriver hon på Facebook. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På fredagen meddelade SD att partiet kan acceptera en borgerlig fyrpartiregering som man självt inte ingår i – och öppnade därmed dörren för Centerpartiet. Centerpartiets Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist höll senare på eftermiddagen en pressträff där hon begärde in varsitt totalpaket från både Magdalena Andersson (S) och Ulf Kristersson (M). I paketen de ska förklara vilken slags regering de ser framför sig och vilken politik de vill föra. I ett långt inlägg på Facebook kommenterar Vänsterpartiets viceordförande Ida Gabrielsson det nya läget. ” Givetvis hoppas jag att C återgår till den positionen dom haft tidigare, dvs står fast vid att de inte låter sig väljas på SD-mandat, och därmed göra sig helt SD-beroende. V inser att det inte blir en total ”vänstersväng” eftersom C:s mandat också kommer att behövas och det har vi också varit tydliga med i våra samtal. ” Centerpartiets öppning har rört upp känslor i det rödgröna lägret. Gabrielsson skriver att hon förstår besvikelsen över utvecklingen. ” Jag förstår oron och besvikelsen som vi är många som känner. V önskar att vi rödgröna gjort mer tillsammans för att C tydligare skulle ha valt det rödgröna regeringsunderlaget innan valet, så att väljare som röstade för att byta ut Tidö visste vad dom röstade på. ” Gabrielsson varnar även Centerpartiet för efterspelet som skulle följa på ett sidbyte från Andersson till Kristersson.
